prompt: ok so we're debating internally whether to switch our python monorepo from unittest to pytest. My take: we should switch, because fixtures beat setUp inheritance, parametrize kills our copy-pasted test variants, and plugins give us xdist parallelism for free. Downsides people raised: 6k existing tests, CI churn, and some devs know unittest well. Can you debate both sides of this properly and give me a recommendation? I get final say.
assertions: The inline proposal is written to a file before the debate so every role argues against the same fixed text
The pro side argues with the user's specifics (fixtures vs setUp inheritance, parametrize vs copy-paste, xdist parallelism)
The con side engages the real costs (6k-test migration, CI churn, team familiarity), not strawmen
The review surfaces that pytest runs existing unittest tests, enabling incremental migration instead of a rewrite
A debate transcript shows distinct role contributions: opening case, objections, defense, rebuttal, and a judge assessment
The output ends with a recommendation and explicitly leaves the final decision to the user
